html:
From 1929 to 1934 Fascist Italy forced most of the people of Cyrenaica, in eastern Libya, into concentration camps in the desert to cut off support for the resistance of Omar Mukhtar.

On the orders of Mussolini's generals, about a hundred thousand people, mostly herders, were marched hundreds of kilometres to camps such as El Agheila. Their flocks were slaughtered. Hunger, disease and executions killed tens of thousands, and the camps broke the herding way of life of the region. A barbed-wire fence some 270 kilometres long was built along the Egyptian border.

Many Libyans call it a genocide. In 2008 Italy apologised and signed a treaty with Gaddafi promising compensation. See also the Senussi order.
sum: From 1929 to 1934 Fascist Italy forced most of the people of Cyrenaica, in eastern Libya, into concentration camps in the desert to cut off support for the resistance of Omar Mukhtar.
